posts.title: Your dev computer, from your phone | Pocket Dev
posts.description:
Your laptop does the work. Your phone gives the commands.

I built Pocket Dev so I could check a coding run, approve the next step, or use a terminal without heading back to my desk.

Claude Code, Codex, Git, files, and real terminals — in your phone's browser, running on your own computer.

Free and open source. Nothing to install on your phone. No Pocket Dev cloud account.

Source and setup: https://github.com/anisirji/pocket-dev

What would you want to do from your phone first?

Demo project shown. Away-from-home access needs optional remote setup; the computer must stay on and awake. Claude Code and Codex use your own accounts.

posts.title: Install Pocket Dev on macOS and connect your phone | Quick start
posts.description:
Install Pocket Dev on your Mac and open your computer's terminal, files, Git and coding agents from your phone.

Current setup note: this recording shows an earlier first-run flow. Today, the first pocket-dev start opens a guided setup before showing the address and QR code. Follow its prompts; pocket-dev setup opens it again later. The install also adds a Pocket Dev Admin shortcut, which this recording does not show.

Requirements: Node.js 22 or newer and a phone on the same Wi-Fi as your Mac.

Install:
npm install -g @anisirji/pocket-dev
pocket-dev start

Current step-by-step guide: https://www.theani.me/work/pocket-dev/docs
Source: https://github.com/anisirji/pocket-dev
